headline: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.voteItem: Motion to substitute Resolution 25-49 with the proposed CD1 version
meeting.summary: The committee voted eight to zero to recommend buying land in Lahaina and deferred Bills 103 and 104.
meeting.recap: Resolution 25-49 would let the County buy a parcel of land in Lahaina.[[0:06:13]] The managing director said other buyers were interested in the property.[[0:13:18]] The managing director said he believed the purchase would use bond money approved for roadway evacuation routes.[[0:17:29]] A council member called the $1.7 million price excessive for an undeveloped half acre.[[0:18:56]] The committee voted eight to zero to recommend adopting the resolution, with one member excused.[[0:26:14]] The Grassroot Institute of Hawaiʻi supported the bill.[[0:57:01]] The fire captain said fire officials cannot require extra fire protection when several homes are built on one lot to code.[[2:17:21]] The committee deferred (put off) Bill 103 with no objections.[[2:49:42]] The committee deferred Bill 104 with no objections.[[2:52:46]] The committee tentatively plans to take up both bills on March 19, with a presentation on "missing middle" housing.[[2:53:04]]
decided: The committee replaced the resolution with a revised version (CD1) that corrects the property owner's names.
The committee deferred Bill 103 with no objections.
The committee deferred Bill 104 with no objections.
meeting.next: Members' written questions will go to the departments so answers can come back before the next meeting.

moments.q: "$1.7 million for an undeveloped half acre is just excessive."

issues.oneLine: The Office of Recovery asked to buy land in Lahaina for a community corridor project in the Lahaina long-term recovery plan.
issues.brief: The chair said this parcel alone would not be enough to create an emergency evacuation route.[[#1]] The managing director said the main reason for buying the land is roadway evacuation routes.[[#2]] The committee voted eight to zero to recommend the purchase.[[#3]]
